findings.title: TEST_EVIDENCE says the 4 critic findings survived verification, but no verifier ever checked them
findings.description: The new TEST_EVIDENCE entry says: "15 of its 16 findings and all 4 critic findings survived verification, and each is corrected." In review-1 only the 16 lens findings went through refuting verifiers, two each. The critic phase ran last and its 4 findings were never verified. The project rule is that records must be exactly true and that nothing may be claimed to have run when it did not. The review packet README (docs/evidence/m03-w07-adr0009-host-closure-review/README.md) states this correctly: "The critic added four, one of them blocking." It makes no verification claim.
findings.evidence: In docs/evidence/m03-w07-adr0009-host-closure-review/review-1-workflow-result.json, workflowProgress counts 32 'Verify' agents (2 x 16 findings), 4 'Review' agents and 1 'Critic' agent. Every result.findings[i] has a two-entry 'verdicts' list. Every result.critic[j] has only the keys ['description','evidence','file','line','severity','title'] and no verdicts. The workflow log is the single line '16 findings, 15 survive at least one refuter'.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute this finding. It is a real, nonblocking records defect.

1. The claim is in the working-tree diff. docs/TEST_EVIDENCE.md line 12734 says: "15 of its 16 findings and all 4 critic findings survived verification, and each is corrected."

2. The review-1 record shows that no verifier checked the critic findings. In docs/evidence/m03-w07-adr0009-host-closure-review/review-1-workflow-result.json:
   - There are three phases in this order: Review, then Verify, then Critic.
   - Grouped by phase, the agents are 4 Review lens agents, 32 Verify agents (10+6+6+10, two per finding), and 1 Critic agent. That makes the agentCount of 37, and no agent ran after the critic.
   - Each of the 16 entries in result.findings has keys 'lens', 'survives' and a two-entry 'verdicts' list.
   - Each of the 4 entries in result.critic has only description, evidence, file, line, severity and title. There are no verdicts and no survives field.
   - The log is the single line "16 findings, 15 survive at least one refuter".
   - The raw task output at tasks/wazmdedze.output has an identical critic array, also without verdicts.

3. Nothing else checked them either:
   - The implementer's dispositions file (scratchpad/review1-dispositions.md) gives fixes for c0–c3. It records no refuting verification of them.
   - The review packet README describes this correctly ("The critic added four, one of them blocking") and makes no verification claim. TEST_EVIDENCE contradicts it.
   - An earlier TEST_EVIDENCE entry (line 12672) has the correct wording: "Every surviving finding and every critic finding is corrected."

The sentence therefore says the critic findings went through a verification step that never ran. That breaks the project rules that records must be exactly true and that nothing may be claimed to have run when it did not. The corrections themselves are not in question; only the wording is wrong. Nonblocking is the right severity.

I could not refute this finding. It reproduces exactly.

1. The sentence is there. The uncommitted TEST_EVIDENCE.md entry "M03-W07 — ADR-0009: the Windows 11 host closure resolves against the runner's dpkg status" (line 12734) says: "15 of its 16 findings and all 4 critic findings survived verification, and each is corrected."

2. The critic findings never went through any verification. I parsed docs/evidence/m03-w07-adr0009-host-closure-review/review-1-workflow-result.json:
   - workflowProgress has three phases in this order: Review, Verify, Critic.
   - The agents per phase are Verify 32, Review 4 and Critic 1. That totals 37, which matches agentCount.
   - The Critic phase ran after Verify.
   - Each of the 16 entries in result.findings has a two-entry verdicts list. One finding, "dpkg_status_sha256 and empty_status_resolution=false never reach the reviewed Wi...", was refuted by both verifiers. That gives 15 surviving, which matches the single log line "16 findings, 15 survive at least one refuter".
   - Each of the 4 entries in result.critic has only the keys description, evidence, file, line, severity and title. None has a verdicts list. No Verify agent ran after the critic.

3. The implementer's own record contradicts the claim. The dispositions file (scratchpad/review1-dispositions.md) shows the implementer accepted and fixed c0 to c3. Nothing in it says any of them were refuted or re-verified. The review packet README states it accurately: "The critic added four, one of them blocking. Each is corrected." It makes no claim that they survived verification. PROJECT_STATUS and KNOWN_ISSUES use the accurate wording "had every surviving finding corrected". Only TEST_EVIDENCE carries the false clause.

4. Could "verification" mean the implementer's own checking? Not in this sentence. The same "survived verification" covers both the 15 lens findings, where it means surviving the workflow's refuting verifiers, and the critic findings. Read that way, it says the critic findings passed the workflow's verifiers, which never happened. The project rules require records to be exactly true and forbid claiming a step ran when it did not. TEST_EVIDENCE specifically must never record what was not run.

The defect is real but nonblocking. The critic findings were all corrected, so this misstates provenance and does not hide a defect. A suggested correction: "15 of its 16 findings survived at least one refuting verifier; the completeness critic added 4 more, which were not separately verified. Each is corrected."

findings.title: The records say every surviving review-1 finding was corrected, but finding 1's ADR-0009 conformance part was only recorded as a limit
findings.evidence: review-1-workflow-result.json findings[1].verdicts[0]: "it means ADR-0009's tradeoff claim, that (B) 'ends the dependency on the archive and the runner image moving in step', does not hold for these two roots. (B) also says a package the image already carries is 'used as installed and not downloaded', yet the code reinstalls or upgrades them." On the real round-52 runner (scratchpad hostclosure-41918821956/art), acl 2.3.2-1build1.1 and python3 3.12.3-0ubuntu2.1 are both in the runner's installed status and in the downloaded lock. resolve() still passes --reinstall (ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py, apt argv).

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute this finding. Every fact it cites checks out, and the records do overstate what was corrected. It is a minor, nonblocking records-accuracy issue.

What I verified:
1. **Finding 1 has both parts.** In review-1-workflow-result.json, finding 1 is titled "Installed HOST_ROOTS (python3, acl) stay tied to the archive, and a root apt cannot reinstall silently drops out...".
   - Its case (2) says an installed root with a newer archive candidate is upgraded and refused.
   - Both verifiers kept that part. One wrote "Net: ... real, and so is the gap in the archive-ahead claim for installed roots". The other said it "does contradict ADR-0009's (B) wording" at DECISIONS.md:470 and :472. Both cited lines are quoted correctly.
2. **The implementer says that part was not fixed.** The disposition (review1-dispositions.md, item 1/8) reads: "The residual (installed roots acl and python3 with a newer archive candidate still fail closed) is recorded as a limit in KI-0189; not fixed."
   - The code agrees. ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py:323 still passes --reinstall, and :406-410 only adds the "Every root must be downloaded" refusal.
   - KI-0189's Limits and the review packet README ("One limit is recorded rather than fixed") say this truthfully.
3. **Three records say every surviving finding was corrected, with no qualification:**
   - KNOWN_ISSUES.md:77: "had every surviving finding corrected; see TEST_EVIDENCE";
   - PROJECT_STATUS.md:90: "had every surviving finding corrected";
   - TEST_EVIDENCE.md:12734: "15 of its 16 findings and all 4 critic findings survived verification, and each is corrected."
4. **The round-52 data matches the finding.** In hostclosure-41918821956/art, runner-dpkg-status shows acl (line 71) and python3 (line 23348) as "install ok installed", and both are in the downloaded closure.

Arguments against the finding, and why they fall short:
- **The limit is disclosed nearby.** KI-0189's Limits list it a few lines below line 77. PROJECT_STATUS points to "Exact KI-0189", and TEST_EVIDENCE points to the review packet. That makes the overstatement easy to discover, but each sentence is still literally false: a surviving finding was only partly corrected, by the implementer's own disposition.
- **The unfixed part fails closed and is safe.** It reinstalls the roots from hashed debs, which is stricter than the ADR requires. That is why this is not a safety defect. It does not make "corrected" true.
- **The "not recorded against ADR-0009" sub-claim is weak.** Changing an ACCEPTED ADR needs owner approval, and KNOWN_ISSUES is the proper place for a deferred limit. The finding's main point, the overbroad "every/each corrected" wording, does not depend on it.

Given the project's rule that records must be exactly true, the finding stands as nonblocking.

I could not refute the finding's main claim. Severity nonblocking is right.

What I verified (read-only, no files touched):

1. Finding 1 had two parts, and both survived.
   - Review-1 finding 1 (review-1-workflow-result.json findings[1]) has a two-part title: "Installed HOST_ROOTS (python3, acl) stay tied to the archive, and a root apt cannot reinstall silently drops out…".
   - Both verifiers returned refuted=false.
   - Verifier 1's net: "the gap in the archive-ahead claim for installed roots" is real, as well as the missing roots check.
   - Verifier 2 called case (2) "a fail-closed limitation against the ADR's stated goal" and said it contradicts ADR-0009 (B)'s wording.

2. Only the silent-drop part was fixed.
   - resolve() now refuses with "Every root must be downloaded: …" (ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py:405-410).
   - The archive-ahead part is unchanged: apt still runs with `--reinstall … install *roots` (:319-330), and no installed root is pinned to the runner's version.
   - The implementer's own disposition says "recorded as a limit in KI-0189; not fixed".
   - The review packet README:26 says "Each is corrected:" and then, at :43, "One limit is recorded rather than fixed".

3. The real round-52 artifact matches the finding.
   - In hostclosure-41918821956/art/runner-dpkg-status the runner carries acl 2.3.2-1build1.1 and python3 3.12.3-0ubuntu2.1.
   - runner-status/lock.json downloads both at those versions.

4. The three summary records say more than the dispositions do.
   - KNOWN_ISSUES.md:77 says "had every surviving finding corrected".
   - PROJECT_STATUS.md:90 says "had every surviving finding corrected".
   - TEST_EVIDENCE.md:12734 says "15 of its 16 findings … survived verification, and each is corrected".
   - Taken literally, all three are false for finding 1's archive-ahead part. Under the project's "records must be exactly true" rule, that is a real records-accuracy defect.

Ways the finding is narrower than stated:
- KNOWN_ISSUES.md is the least misleading of the three. Its own Limits list, at :81, states the acl/python3 residual a few lines below the claim.
- PROJECT_STATUS:90 and TEST_EVIDENCE:12734 do not mention the limit. They only point to KI-0189 and the review packet, which do.
- The sub-claim that the ADR deviation should be recorded "against ADR-0009" is weaker.
  - Downloading the installed roots is stricter than (B), because more packages are hashed.
  - The behaviour fails closed.
  - ADR-0009 is owner-ACCEPTED text, so the implementer could not just edit it. Recording the limit in KI-0189 is a reasonable place for it.
  - Still, the tradeoff claim that (B) "ends the dependency on the archive and the runner image moving in step" does not hold for these two roots, and no ADR-level note says so.

Net: the core claim stands. Three status records state an unqualified "every surviving finding corrected" or "each is corrected" while one surviving part was only recorded as a limit. It is not a safety issue.

findings.title: Disposition 14 leaves the copy-time oversize bound on the runner status untested; removing that cap survives
findings.description:
Review-1 finding 14 named "the copy-time sha(DPKG_STATUS, DPKG_STATUS_CAP) non-regular/oversize refusal in resolve" as untested. The disposition added two tests:
- the symlink test, which covers the non-regular half;
- a byte-cap test, which only covers runner_provided()'s later `len(raw) > DPKG_STATUS_CAP` check.
No test covers the oversize half of the copy-time check. If the cap is dropped from the pre-copy call, every test still passes. The impact is limited: an oversize status is copied and apt runs against it before resolve()'s later `sha(root / "status", DPKG_STATUS_CAP)` refuses. So the prepare still fails closed, only later. The disposition's "status byte cap" does not cover the check finding 14 named.
findings.evidence: In my own copy (review2-work/dispositions/copy3) I applied the mutant `sha(DPKG_STATUS, DPKG_STATUS_CAP)` -> `sha(DPKG_STATUS)` at ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py:312. Running tools/extra_mutants.py, which runs pytest on scripts/tests/test_ubuntu_gnome_review_regressions.py, gave `x_copy_time_cap_removed: SURVIVED | 37 passed in 0.27s`. In the same run, the control mutants for the other dispositions (no-colon refusal removed, absent-key default [], post-check moved before the install, root check only on the first root, stage_host runner rows emptied) were all KILLED.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute this finding. It reproduces, and it accurately describes a gap left by disposition 14.

Code: ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py:312 calls `sha(DPKG_STATUS, DPKG_STATUS_CAP)` before the copy. `sha` (ubuntu_gnome_vm.py:123) refuses a file that is not regular or whose size is over the cap, and its default cap is 1 GiB. DPKG_STATUS_CAP is 64 MiB. If the cap argument is dropped, a status between 64 MiB and 1 GiB passes the copy-time check. It is then copied, and `apt-get update` and the download both run against it. Only afterwards does line 411, `sha(root / "status", DPKG_STATUS_CAP)`, refuse it, and runner_provided's `len(raw) > DPKG_STATUS_CAP` would also refuse it. So the prepare still fails closed, only later. That matches the finding's "nonblocking" severity.

Review-1 finding 14 named "the copy-time sha(DPKG_STATUS, DPKG_STATUS_CAP) non-regular/oversize refusal in resolve" separately from the "Bounded runner dpkg status required" bound. The disposition covered them as follows:
- **The runner_provided bound:** covered by test_runner_provided_is_finite[status-bytes], which calls runner_provided directly.
- **The copy-time check:** covered only by test_resolve_refuses_a_runner_status_that_is_not_a_bounded_regular_file. Despite its name, that test passes a symlink, so `S_ISREG` refuses it whatever the cap is.

The committed mutants.py has p_no_symlink_refusal, which removes the whole sha call and is killed. It has no mutant that drops only the cap argument.

Reproduction, in my own copy at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-tanishkalwad-jobapplyv2/17ee071f-b2d5-4e6f-a57e-209b35ae06c1/scratchpad/review2-work/refute-d14-cap/copy:
- **The mutant survives.** I applied `sha(DPKG_STATUS, DPKG_STATUS_CAP)` -> `sha(DPKG_STATUS)` at line 312 and ran every test file that references the prepare or the candidate: test_ubuntu_gnome_review_regressions, test_ubuntu_gnome_boundaries and test_windows11_host_runtime. Result: 161 passed, 0 failed.
- **The gap is testable.** I wrote a probe test that monkeypatches DPKG_STATUS_CAP to 64 and gives resolve an Owner that refuses any command. It passes on the original source and fails on the mutant with "No command may run".

Nothing in the record contradicts the finding. The defect is real but minor: a test-coverage gap with a later fail-closed backstop. Disposition 14's "status byte cap" covers a different check from the copy-time oversize refusal.

I could not refute the finding. I reproduced it independently.

Code: in resolve(), at scripts/linux_gnome/ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py:312, `sha(DPKG_STATUS, DPKG_STATUS_CAP)` runs before `shutil.copyfile(DPKG_STATUS, root / "status")` and before any apt command. sha() (ubuntu_gnome_vm.py:123) refuses on two conditions: a non-regular file, or a size over the cap. If no cap is passed, it defaults to 1 GiB.

What the tests cover:
- `test_resolve_refuses_a_runner_status_that_is_not_a_bounded_regular_file` uses a symlink, so it reaches only the non-regular arm.
- `test_runner_provided_is_finite[status-bytes]` monkeypatches DPKG_STATUS_CAP=64 but calls runner_provided() directly. It reaches only the later `len(raw) > DPKG_STATUS_CAP` check at line 232, never resolve().
- mutants.py has p_no_symlink_refusal, which deletes the whole sha call and is killed. It has no mutant that drops only the cap argument.

What I ran, in my own copy (review2-work/refute-copycap/copy, made with rsync from scripts, pyproject.toml and .github):
- I applied `sha(DPKG_STATUS, DPKG_STATUS_CAP)` -> `sha(DPKG_STATUS)`.
- test_ubuntu_gnome_review_regressions.py plus test_windows11_host_runtime.py gave 125 passed.
- test_ubuntu_gnome_boundaries.py, the only other test file that loads the prepare module, gave 36 passed.
- So the mutant survives every test that reaches this code.

I then wrote a probe in my copy. It reuses resolve_fixture with DPKG_STATUS_CAP=64 and runner_status=True.
- Original code: it refuses with "Bounded regular input required" before the copy. The private status stays the fixture's empty bytes, and the probe passes.
- Mutant: the oversize runner status is copied and apt update/install run against it. The run is refused only later, at line 411's `sha(root / "status", DPKG_STATUS_CAP)`, with the same message. The probe fails.
- So a simple test would kill the mutant, and none exists.

Impact: the finding's assessment is accurate. The prepare still fails closed, just after apt has run on the oversize copy. That makes it a nonblocking coverage gap, not a safety hole.

Why this still counts:
- Review-1 finding 14 explicitly named "the copy-time sha(DPKG_STATUS, DPKG_STATUS_CAP) non-regular/oversize refusal in resolve".
- Disposition 14 lists "status byte cap" and "symlinked status". Neither reaches the copy-time oversize arm.
- The README in docs/evidence/m03-w07-adr0009-host-closure-review and PROJECT_STATUS/KNOWN_ISSUES say every surviving finding was corrected. That overstates finding 14 slightly.

The finding is accurate, reproducible and not already handled.

findings.title: No campaign test feeds an architecture 'all' runner-provided row, so a regression that refuses every real lock goes undetected
findings.description: The code is correct today: runner_packages() keeps amd64 and all instances, matching the prepare's RUNNER_ARCHITECTURES. The gap is in the tests. Every runner-provided fixture in scripts/tests/test_windows11_host_runtime.py (RUNNER_PROVIDED at line 254, INSTALLED at line 314, and the drift and held cases) uses architecture 'amd64'. The real lock is different: in the round-52 runner-status lock (docs/evidence/m03-native-runtime-diagnostics/windows-host-closure/round52-41918821956/runner-status-lock.json), 10 of the 88 runner-provided rows are 'all': adduser, debconf, libasound2-data, libaudit-common, libjson-glib-1.0-common, libsemanage-common, media-types, netbase, readline-common and tzdata. Suppose the campaign's filter narrowed to amd64. Every 'all' row would then drop out of the live result, and require_runner_packages would refuse every real candidate with 'Runner-provided host packages differ from the reviewed lock'. The whole suite would still pass. The prepare side does test an 'all' row (test_ubuntu_gnome_review_regressions.py lines 259 and 294); the campaign side does not. This fails closed, so it is not a safety problem, but it would only show up during a released campaign. Fix: add an 'all' runner-provided row (for example tzdata) to one before-and-after campaign test.
findings.evidence: I ran my own mutants on a separate copy (scratchpad/review2-work/candidate-campaign/copy, with my_mutants.py beside it) using the repository's .venv Python. Mutant w_all_arch_refused, which changes windows11_vm.py:302 from `if arch not in {"amd64", "all"}:` to `if arch not in {"amd64"}:`, gave 'SURVIVED | 88 passed in 23.12s'. Mutant w_arch_not_compared, which forces the architecture to 'amd64' on both sides of the comparison, also survived (88 passed). That second case matters less, because a package keeping its version while changing architecture is practically unreachable. The other nine reviewer mutants were killed: pre-check moved after the simulated install, pre-check moved after the real install, rows dropped from host-tools.json, version not compared, candidate rows not staged, schema left at v1, status retained in private-work, and status retained in inputs. w_subset_compare also survived, but it is equivalent to the original because dpkg-query returns only the queried names. Running `grep -n '"all"' scripts/tests/test_windows11_host_runtime.py` finds nothing.

verdicts.reasoning:
I tried to refute this finding and could not. Every claim in it checks out.

(1) Code. In scripts/windows11/windows11_vm.py, line 302 of runner_packages reads `if arch not in {"amd64", "all"}: continue`. This matches RUNNER_ARCHITECTURES = frozenset({"amd64", "all"}) in ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py:77, so the code is correct today, as the finding says.

(2) Real lock shape. Parsing docs/evidence/m03-native-runtime-diagnostics/windows-host-closure/round52-41918821956/runner-status-lock.json gives 88 runner_provided_packages. Ten of them are architecture 'all': adduser, debconf, libasound2-data, libaudit-common, libjson-glib-1.0-common, libsemanage-common, media-types, netbase, readline-common and tzdata. That is the exact list in the finding.

(3) Test fixtures. In scripts/tests/test_windows11_host_runtime.py, RUNNER_PROVIDED (line 254), INSTALLED (line 314) and the held, drift and refusal parametrizations use only 'amd64', plus one 'i386' foreign instance. `grep -rln '"all"'` over scripts/tests matches only test_ubuntu_gnome_review_regressions.py, which is the prepare side. Of the other test files that import windows11_vm (boot_console, artifact_layout, local_apt, guest_driver, isolation), none references runner_packages or install_tools.

(4) Mutant reproduced. My own copy is at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-tanishkalwad-jobapplyv2/17ee071f-b2d5-4e6f-a57e-209b35ae06c1/scratchpad/review2-work/refute-all-arch/copy, with scripts, pyproject.toml and .github. I changed line 302 to `if arch not in {"amd64"}:`. test_windows11_host_runtime.py then gave "88 passed in 22.96s", so the mutant SURVIVED. An earlier run without .github showed one failure in the lifecycle-timeout test; that failure was environmental and unrelated.

(5) Not already handled. The committed mutants.py (docs/evidence/m03-w07-adr0009-host-closure-review/mutants.py) has w_foreign_counted, which deletes the whole filter, but no mutant that narrows it to amd64 only. review1-dispositions.md does not address 'all'-architecture coverage either.

Consequence. A regression that narrowed the filter would make the live dict miss the 10 'all' rows. require_runner_packages would then refuse every real lock with "Runner-provided host packages differ from the reviewed lock". This fails closed, so it is not a safety issue, and the severity of nonblocking fits. But the suite would not detect it, and it would only show up on a released hosted campaign. This is a real test-coverage gap.

I could not refute this finding. It is a real, reproducible test gap. It is not a code defect, and it is nonblocking because it fails closed.

1. **The code is correct today.** The uncommitted diff of scripts/windows11/windows11_vm.py adds `runner_packages()`. At line 302 it keeps rows whose architecture is in `{"amd64", "all"}`. `require_runner_packages` then requires the live (version, arch, status) map to equal the reviewed one exactly, both before the simulated install and after the real one.

2. **No campaign test uses an 'all' row.** In scripts/tests/test_windows11_host_runtime.py, every runner-provided fixture uses "amd64" or a foreign "i386" instance. That covers RUNNER_PROVIDED (line 254), INSTALLED (line 314), the before-and-after test, the held test, the change-during-install test and the drift parametrization. `grep -rn '"all"' scripts/tests` finds only test_ubuntu_gnome_review_regressions.py:294, which is on the prepare side.

3. **The real lock does contain 'all' rows.** I loaded docs/evidence/m03-native-runtime-diagnostics/windows-host-closure/round52-41918821956/runner-status-lock.json. It has 88 runner_provided_packages: 78 amd64 and 10 'all'. The 'all' rows are adduser, debconf, libasound2-data, libaudit-common, libjson-glib-1.0-common, libsemanage-common, media-types, netbase, readline-common and tzdata, exactly as the finding states.

4. **The mutant survives.** I made my own copy at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-tanishkalwad-jobapplyv2/17ee071f-b2d5-4e6f-a57e-209b35ae06c1/scratchpad/review2-work/refute-all-arch/copy and changed line 302 to `if arch not in {"amd64"}:`. `pytest scripts/tests/test_windows11_host_runtime.py` then gave "88 passed in 22.89s".
   - With that mutant, every 'all' row would drop out of the live map. The pre-check would then raise "Runner-provided host packages differ from the reviewed lock" on every real candidate, and no test catches it.
   - I also ran every test file that references windows11_vm or windows11_candidate against the mutant: 2 failed and 16 errored. I only inspected the message summary, not each failing test. Every message I saw was FileNotFoundError for package.json, which my partial copy leaves out, and none mentioned the runner-package check.

5. **Not already handled.** The committed mutant list (docs/evidence/m03-w07-adr0009-host-closure-review/mutants.py and mutants-result.txt) includes w_foreign_counted, which removes the filter. It has no mutant that narrows the filter to amd64. review1-dispositions.md does not mention 'all'-architecture coverage on the campaign side.

**Impact:** the gap is safe, since a regression would only refuse candidates and would never accept a bad one. But a regression would go undetected until a hosted campaign run. The suggested fix is a regression test, not a weakening: add an 'all' runner-provided row such as tzdata to one before-and-after campaign test.

findings.title: TEST_EVIDENCE says the 4 critic findings 'survived verification', but the workflow never verified them
findings.description: The record says '15 of its 16 findings and all 4 critic findings survived verification, and each is corrected.' In wf_8b1c4c96-433 the Critic phase (phase 3) ran after the Verify phase (phase 2). None of the 4 critic findings has a `verdicts` or `survives` field, and no verify agent was launched for them. This is a claim that verification ran when it did not. The review packet README (line 26) is accurate: 'The critic added four, one of them blocking.'
findings.evidence: review-1-workflow-result.json: result.critic[*] keys are only ['title','file','line','severity','description','evidence']. workflowProgress lists phases Review → Verify → Critic. Agents 5–36 are all 'verify:<lens>:<finding>:<n>' over the 16 lens findings, and agent 37 is 'critic' with no verify agents after it. logs[0] = '16 findings, 15 survive at least one refuter'.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute this finding. The sentence is false as written and is still in the working tree.

1. The claim is present. docs/TEST_EVIDENCE.md line 12734 (an added line in the uncommitted diff) says: "15 of its 16 findings and all 4 critic findings survived verification, and each is corrected."

2. The workflow record shows that no verification ran on the critic findings. I read docs/evidence/m03-w07-adr0009-host-closure-review/review-1-workflow-result.json.
   - workflowProgress lists three phases in this order: Review (1), Verify (2), Critic (3).
   - agentCount is 37, made up of:
     - agents 1-4: `review:<lens>`;
     - agents 5-36: `verify:<lens>:<finding>:<n>`, two refuters for each of the 16 lens findings (5+5+3+3 = 16 findings, 32 verifiers);
     - agent 37: `critic`, in the Critic phase. Its start time is after the last verifier finished, and no agent follows it.
   - Each of the 16 entries in result.findings has `verdicts` and `survives` fields. One has survives=False, which matches "15 of 16".
   - Each of the 4 entries in result.critic has only title, file, line, severity, description and evidence. There are no verdicts and no survives field.
   - logs is exactly ['16 findings, 15 survive at least one refuter'], so the critic findings are not counted in any survival tally.

3. Nothing else in the record turns this into verification. The implementer's dispositions file (scratchpad/review1-dispositions.md) only maps c0-c3 to corrections. It records no refutation or reproduction pass over the critic findings. The critic's own evidence (its mutant run for c0, its grep for c1) is the finder's own support, not a verification pass. The review packet README describes this correctly: "The critic added four, one of them blocking. Each is corrected." So the repository's own packet already contradicts the TEST_EVIDENCE wording.

4. Project rules: TEST_EVIDENCE must never record something that did not run, and records must be exactly true. "Survived verification" claims that a verification step ran on the 4 critic findings, and it did not. The other parts of the sentence are true: 15 of 16 survived, and each finding has a recorded correction. The defect is only the "all 4 critic findings survived verification" clause. It should say something like "the critic added four more, which were not separately verified; each of the 20 is corrected."

The finding is accurate, reproducible from the retained JSON, and not yet handled.

I could not refute this finding. Every part of it checks out against the retained record.

1. **The sentence is there.** docs/TEST_EVIDENCE.md line 12734 (uncommitted diff) says: "15 of its 16 findings and all 4 critic findings survived verification, and each is corrected."

2. **No verification step ran on the critic findings.** In docs/evidence/m03-w07-adr0009-host-closure-review/review-1-workflow-result.json:
   - workflowProgress has three phases in order: Review (1), Verify (2), Critic (3).
   - Agents 1-4 are the review lenses. Agents 5-36 are all `verify:<lens>:<i>:<j>`, two per lens finding over the 16 lens findings. Agent 37 is `critic` in phase 3, and no agent runs after it. agentCount is 37.
   - Each of the 16 entries in result.findings has `lens`, `survives` and `verdicts` keys. Each of the 4 entries in result.critic has only `title`, `file`, `line`, `severity`, `description` and `evidence`. There is no `verdicts` or `survives` key.
   - logs[0] is "16 findings, 15 survive at least one refuter". It counts only the lens findings.

3. **Nothing else describes a verification of them.** The implementer's dispositions file (scratchpad/review1-dispositions.md) maps c0-c3 straight to corrections and records no refuter or verification of the critic findings. The review packet README line 26 says it accurately: "The critic added four, one of them blocking."

The part about the 16 lens findings (15 survived) is correct. The claim that "all 4 critic findings survived verification" says a verification ran that did not. That breaks the project rules "never claim something ran when it did not" and "records must be exactly true". The defect is real. Rewording the sentence to match the README (the critic added four findings, and each is corrected) would fix it. I made no edits.

findings.title: 'Every surviving finding corrected' overstates: part of surviving finding 1 is recorded as a limit, not fixed
findings.description: PROJECT_STATUS:90 and KNOWN_ISSUES.md:77 say wf_8b1c4c96-433 'had every surviving finding corrected'. TEST_EVIDENCE.md:12734 says 'each is corrected'. Surviving finding 1 has two parts. Its silent-drop part was fixed with the every-root refusal. Its other part was not fixed: installed roots python3 and acl still fail the prepare when the archive is ahead of the image. The packet README (line 43) says 'One limit is recorded rather than fixed', and the implementer's dispositions say 'recorded as a limit in KI-0189; not fixed'. The three summary sentences contradict that.
findings.evidence: review-1-workflow-result.json findings[1] (survives: true), title 'Installed HOST_ROOTS (python3, acl) stay tied to the archive ...'. Its description says: 'the archive-ahead-of-image failure that ADR-0009 says it ends still applies to installed roots'. review1-dispositions.md item 1/8 says: 'The residual ... is recorded as a limit in KI-0189; not fixed.'

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute this finding. Every part of it checks out against the working tree and the review-1 record.

1. **The summary sentences say what the finding quotes.**
   - docs/PROJECT_STATUS.md:90 says the review "had every surviving finding corrected".
   - docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md:77 (KI-0189) says the same, with "see TEST_EVIDENCE".
   - docs/TEST_EVIDENCE.md:12734 says "15 of its 16 findings and all 4 critic findings survived verification, and each is corrected".
   - Nothing else in the TEST_EVIDENCE section (12718-12745) mentions the acl/python3 limit. PROJECT_STATUS:90 does not mention it either.

2. **Surviving finding 1 has two parts, and the first was not fixed.**
   - In review-1-workflow-result.json, result.findings[1] has survives=true. Its title is "Installed HOST_ROOTS (python3, acl) stay tied to the archive, and a root apt cannot reinstall silently drops out...".
   - Case (2) of its description is the part that was not fixed. When the archive's candidate is newer, the root is upgraded and the plan is refused, so "the archive-ahead-of-image failure that ADR-0009 says it ends still applies to installed roots".
   - Both refuter verdicts confirm case (2) as real. They call it "a fail-closed limitation against the ADR's stated goal" and a "nonblocking hardening point".

3. **The implementer's own records say that part is a limit, not a fix.**
   - review1-dispositions.md item 1/8 fixes only the silent-drop part, with the every-root refusal. It says the residual "is recorded as a limit in KI-0189; not fixed."
   - The review packet README (line 43) says "One limit is recorded rather than fixed".
   - KI-0189's Limits list says the same about acl and python3.
   - The ADR-0009 text still says (B) "ends the dependency on the archive and the runner image moving in step", unchanged.

4. **Possible refutation considered and rejected.** One could argue that case (2) fails closed, so it is a limitation rather than a defect. But the reviewers made it part of the surviving finding, and the project's own packet calls it unfixed. So "every surviving finding corrected" and "each is corrected" overstate what was done. Under the "records must be exactly true" rule, this is a real but nonblocking records inconsistency. KI-0189's own Limits list, a few lines below its claim, contradicts it. PROJECT_STATUS and TEST_EVIDENCE give no qualification at all.

I could not refute this finding. The overstatement is real and nonblocking is the right severity.

1. Surviving finding 1 has two parts. In review-1-workflow-result.json, findings[1] is titled "Installed HOST_ROOTS (python3, acl) stay tied to the archive, and a root apt cannot reinstall silently drops out...". Both verdicts left it unrefuted. Part (a) says that when the archive is ahead of the image, an installed root is upgraded and the simulated install refuses the plan. That means the archive-ahead failure ADR-0009 says it ends still applies to roots. ADR-0009's Tradeoffs line does say "(B) ends the dependency on the archive and the runner image moving in step."

2. Only part (b) was fixed. ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py:410 now raises "Every root must be downloaded". Part (a) is unchanged:
   - resolve still passes --reinstall (line 323).
   - HOST_ROOTS in windows11_candidate.py:40-51 still contains acl and python3.
   - PLAN_ADD (ubuntu_gnome_host.py:55) still refuses the upgrade form "Inst X [old] (new ...)".
   The implementer's dispositions (item 1/8) say: "The residual ... is recorded as a limit in KI-0189; not fixed." KNOWN_ISSUES.md:81 and the review packet README:43 ("One limit is recorded rather than fixed") say the same.

3. Several summary sentences claim everything was corrected:
   - PROJECT_STATUS.md:90: "had every surviving finding corrected". Nothing in that bullet mentions the limit.
   - TEST_EVIDENCE.md:12734: "15 of its 16 findings and all 4 critic findings survived verification, and each is corrected". That section does not mention the acl/python3 limit either. A grep of the TEST_EVIDENCE diff finds no acl/limit text.
   - KNOWN_ISSUES.md:77: "had every surviving finding corrected; see TEST_EVIDENCE". The same entry does disclose the limit four lines later, at :81, which softens this one but does not make the sentence true.
   - README:26 also says "Each is corrected:", which contradicts its own line 43.

Under the project's rule that records must be exactly true, "every surviving finding corrected" and "each is corrected" are not exactly true. Part of one surviving finding was knowingly recorded as a limit, not corrected. The defect is in the records only: the code fails closed, and the limit is disclosed in KI-0189 and the packet. So the finding is valid and nonblocking. A fix would say something like "every surviving finding was corrected except the installed-root residual of finding 1, recorded as a KI-0189 limit" in PROJECT_STATUS:90, TEST_EVIDENCE:12734, KNOWN_ISSUES:77 and README:26.

findings.title: The local mutant pass is listed as one of the real-runner rounds' results
findings.description: Line 12736 opens a list: 'Rounds 51 (...) and 52 (...) gave the same results:'. The fourth bullet of that list (line 12740) is 'The final mutant pass (mutants.py on a fresh copy of the working tree) killed all 52 mutants'. That pass was a local run, not a result of the hosted rounds, so the record attributes it to runs that did not produce it. The bullet belongs with the review/mutation sentence at line 12734 or the commands list.
findings.evidence: TEST_EVIDENCE.md lines 12736-12740. The mutant pass ran locally: mutants-result.txt is dated 16:59 local, after round 52 finished at 21:45Z (16:45 local), and mutants.py runs pytest on a local copy only.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute this finding. It is a real but nonblocking records defect.

1. **The bullet sits under a list that credits both runs.** Line 12736 of the uncommitted docs/TEST_EVIDENCE.md says "Rounds 51 (run 41912040314, ..., pre-review code) and 52 (run 41918821956, ..., the current sources) gave the same results:". Bullet 4 of that list, at line 12740, is "The final mutant pass (...mutants.py on a fresh copy of the working tree) killed all 52 mutants (mutants-result.txt)". The diff confirms both lines are new in this change.

2. **Neither hosted round ran the mutants.**
   - The round 52 artifacts (scratchpad hostclosure-41918821956/art) hold only empty-status/, runner-status/, runner-dpkg-status and summary.json.
   - grep finds "mutant" nowhere in either round's downloaded artifacts or in the retained docs/evidence/m03-native-runtime-diagnostics/windows-host-closure/ records.
   - mutants.py says it applies edits to a local copy and runs pytest there.
   - mutants-result.txt has mtime 16:59 local, after round 52 finished.

3. **The claim cannot be true for round 51.** Round 51 ran pre-review code. The final 52/52 result depends on test changes made after the review; before them only 50 of 52 were killed, as line 12734 and the review README say. Read as written, "gave the same results" says round 51 also killed all 52 mutants, which is false.

4. **Mitigation, not a refutation.** The bullet's own wording ("on a fresh copy of the working tree") and the review README's Mutation section, which describes the pass as a local pass over the sources and tests as committed, do hint that the pass was local. But the TEST_EVIDENCE list still credits the result to the wrong runs, and records must be exactly true.

**Fix:** move the bullet next to the review and mutation sentence at line 12734, or into the commands list.

I could not refute this finding. In the uncommitted addition to /Users/tanishkalwad/jobapplyv2/docs/TEST_EVIDENCE.md (the ADR-0009 section near lines 12736-12740), one sentence introduces a list: "Rounds 51 (run 41912040314, ...) and 52 (run 41918821956, ...) gave the same results:". That list has four bullets, and the fourth reads "The final mutant pass (docs/evidence/m03-w07-adr0009-host-closure-review/mutants.py on a fresh copy of the working tree) killed all 52 mutants (mutants-result.txt)". Because of where it sits, that bullet says the hosted diagnostic rounds produced the mutant result.

findings.title: Copy-time size bound on the runner dpkg status is untested although the test name claims it
findings.description: resolve(runner_status=True) runs `sha(DPKG_STATUS, DPKG_STATUS_CAP)` before it copies the status and runs apt (ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py:312). test_resolve_refuses_a_runner_status_that_is_not_a_bounded_regular_file only uses a symlink, so it proves 'regular' and not 'bounded'. The byte-cap test (test_runner_provided_is_finite[status-bytes]) calls runner_provided() directly, not resolve(). With the cap removed at copy time, an oversized live status would be copied and used for apt update and the download. It would be refused only afterwards, by sha(root / "status", DPKG_STATUS_CAP). It still fails closed, but later than the code comment ('A bounded regular file, copied') says. Suggested fix: add a resolve-level case that monkeypatches DPKG_STATUS_CAP below the fixture size and asserts no command ran.
findings.evidence: My own mutant x_copy_cap_dropped replaced `        sha(DPKG_STATUS, DPKG_STATUS_CAP)\n` with `        sha(DPKG_STATUS)\n`. Result: `x_copy_cap_dropped: SURVIVED | 37 passed in 0.25s` on test_ubuntu_gnome_review_regressions.py.

I could not refute this finding. It is a real test-coverage gap and nonblocking is the right severity.

1. **The code.** `resolve(runner_status=True)` at `scripts/linux_gnome/ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py:312` calls `sha(DPKG_STATUS, DPKG_STATUS_CAP)` before `shutil.copyfile` and before both apt-get commands. `sha` is defined at `scripts/linux_gnome/ubuntu_gnome_vm.py:123`. It refuses a file that is not regular or is larger than the cap, and its default cap is 1 GiB. Dropping the argument therefore loosens the copy-time bound from 64 MiB to 1 GiB without removing the regular-file check.

2. **The resolve-level test.** `test_resolve_refuses_a_runner_status_that_is_not_a_bounded_regular_file` (line 643) uses only a symlink. It therefore covers the regular-file branch and never the size branch.

3. **The byte-cap test.** `test_runner_provided_is_finite[status-bytes]` lowers `DPKG_STATUS_CAP` but calls `runner_provided()` directly, so the copy-time check in `resolve` is never reached.

4. **The only other caller.** The one other test that mentions `runner_status`, in `test_windows11_host_runtime.py` around line 814, replaces `resolve` with a mock.

5. **The project's mutant set.** `docs/evidence/m03-w07-adr0009-host-closure-review/mutants.py` has `p_no_symlink_refusal`, which deletes the whole `sha` line, and `p_status_cap_removed`, which targets the check inside `runner_provided`. It has no mutant that removes only the copy-time cap.

**Reproduction.** I made my own copy at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-tanishkalwad-jobapplyv2/17ee071f-b2d5-4e6f-a57e-209b35ae06c1/scratchpad/review2-work/refute-copy-cap/copy`. There I changed the line to `sha(DPKG_STATUS)`. The mutant survived:

findings.title: Windows RunnerOwner cannot model a purged runner-provided package; that realistic drift is untested
findings.description: The campaign-side fake answers dpkg-query with `instances = self.runner[name]`, which raises KeyError for a name with no instance. Real dpkg-query -W exits 1 for such a name ('no packages found matching'), and the shared Owner then raises RuntimeError('Owned command failed; original raw output retained'). The GNOME-side DpkgQueryOwner models this; RunnerOwner does not. The drift case named 'removed' (line 471) is really a 'deinstall ok config-files' (rc) row, which dpkg-query still prints. The case a newer runner image would most likely produce, a purged package that is absent entirely, is therefore never exercised. Nothing proves that install_tools refuses it before any apt command. The code does fail closed through the real Owner. The gap is test fidelity and coverage only.
findings.evidence: test_windows11_host_runtime.py:295 `instances = self.runner[name]` (KeyError for unknown names). Line 471: `(("10.42-4ubuntu2.1", "amd64", "deinstall ok config-files"), NOT_ONCE)` is the only 'removed' case. Contrast DpkgQueryOwner in test_ubuntu_gnome_review_regressions.py: `if any(name not in {row[0] for row in self.live} for name in names): raise RuntimeError("Owned command failed; no packages found matching")`.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute this finding. Every factual claim holds, and the finding is correctly rated nonblocking (a test gap, not a code defect).

1. **The fake cannot model a purged package.** `RunnerOwner.command` (scripts/tests/test_windows11_host_runtime.py:295) does `instances = self.runner[name]` and has no exit-status path. I wrote a probe in my own copy (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-tanishkalwad-jobapplyv2/17ee071f-b2d5-4e6f-a57e-209b35ae06c1/scratchpad/review2-work/tests-purged-refuter/copy/scripts/tests/test_zz_purged_probe.py). It removes libpcre2-8-0 from the runner table while the lock still names it. `windows_install` then raises KeyError from the fake, not a refusal from the code under test.

critic.title: No test checks that the runner-provided walk and its status hash read the private copy apt resolved against, not the live /var/lib/dpkg/status
critic.description: With runner_status=True, resolve() copies DPKG_STATUS to root/status. apt resolves against that copy, and the candidate retains it as runner-dpkg-status. resolve() then hashes the copy (dpkg_status_sha256) and walks it (runner_provided(owner, root / "status", controls)). KI-0189 says this is what lets a reviewer recompute the list from the retained file. resolve_fixture points DPKG_STATUS at a file whose bytes equal the copy and never changes it after the copy. So a regression that walks and hashes the live status instead goes unnoticed. The lock's runner_provided_packages could then come from a different file than the one apt used and the candidate retains. The live dpkg-query cross-check would not catch this, because it agrees with the live file too. The candidate's runtime digest check catches a hash of the live file only when the live file has changed, and it never catches the walk reading the live file. This is a separate gap from the listed ones: the copy-time cap, the GNOME default and the copy-before-apt ordering, which only pins what apt sees.
critic.evidence: In my own copy (scratchpad/review2-work/critic/mcopy), I replaced runner_provided(owner, root / "status", controls) with runner_provided(owner, DPKG_STATUS, controls): scripts/tests/test_ubuntu_gnome_review_regressions.py gave '37 passed' (SURVIVED). That replacement plus sha(root / "status", ...) -> sha(DPKG_STATUS, ...) for dpkg_status_sha256 also gave '37 passed'. Fixture: test_ubuntu_gnome_review_regressions.py:580-581 (runner.write_bytes(RUNNER_STATUS.encode()); monkeypatch DPKG_STATUS) and nothing alters it after the copy. A killing test would have the fake apt-get update rewrite the live DPKG_STATUS, for example drop libgcc-s1, and assert that the lock still records libgcc-s1 from the copy.

critic.title: A runner-status walk refusal leaves the candidate unable to show which runner package caused it: the status copy is deleted and the messages name no package
critic.description: The new failure modes of the Windows prepare happen inside resolve(): a live dpkg mismatch, a duplicate installed package, or a malformed status paragraph or continuation. When one raises, main() never reaches the copy to args.output/runner-dpkg-status, which runs only after resolve returns. The finally block then runs shutil.rmtree(work), deleting private-work/apt/status, and retain() also skips private-work. Three of these refusals name no package and no line: 'Runner dpkg database differs from its copied status', 'Duplicate installed runner package' and 'Malformed Debian control paragraph'. The live dpkg-query stdout is retained as a command record, but the copied side it was compared with is not. A future prepare that fails this way, for example from one unrelated package on a new image (the class review-1 finding 0 was about), therefore needs another scratch round to diagnose. KI-0189 itself was diagnosable from its candidate: closed_install_plan names the refused plan lines, and KI-0189's Reproduction line cites them.
critic.evidence: windows11_candidate.py:330-333: lock = resolve(...runner_status=True), then shutil.copyfile(work / "apt" / "status", args.output / "runner-dpkg-status"), which runs only on success. windows11_candidate.py:416: shutil.rmtree(work) in the finally block. windows11_inputs.py:447: retain() skips the 'private-work' and 'retained' directories. ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py:169, 214 and 268: refusal texts with no package or line named. ubuntu_gnome_host.closed_install_plan names its refused plan lines instead ('replace or remove runner packages: ' + '; '.join(refused[:6])).

critic.title: The parser fix's tolerance of non-UTF-8 bytes in the runner status and dpkg-query output is not pinned by any test
critic.description: Disposition 0 made the runner-status parser accept everything dpkg accepts, because one unrelated runner package could otherwise fail every candidate. installed_status() decodes the whole runner status with errors='replace', and installed_rows() does the same for dpkg-query. dpkg does not require UTF-8 in status fields, and runner images carry third-party packages. The fixture has \x0c and U+2028 but only valid UTF-8, so a regression to strict decode reintroduces the 'one unrelated package fails every candidate' class with no failing test. The current images' status is valid UTF-8 (checked on round 52), so nothing fails today. This is a test gap only.
